headline: High-risk pair: Devin’s broad shell/network/write access can collide with next-ai-draw-io’s API-driven document processing, creating default-path data leakage and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin ingests files, MCP, Slack, and browser content, while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs/text/images and uses MCP plus browser-based AI flows. A shared workspace or copied document can carry attacker-controlled instructions into Devin’s autonomous agent loop. The interaction is plausible but not directly documented, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Devin reads next-ai-draw-io output from a shared file or MCP channel without provenance checks, prompt injection is possible.
IF next-ai-draw-io forwards untrusted document text into Devin-facing instructions, the attack path exists.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces and disable shared file mounts.
Require provenance tags on all cross-agent content.
Strip instructions from imported documents before Devin reads them.
Restrict MCP endpoints to allowlisted schemas.
requires-engineering: add content-safety filtering between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin handles repo clones, cloud workspace files, and secrets such as deploy keys and integration tokens, with broad network egress and write access. next-ai-draw-io sends content to multiple third-party model APIs by default. If the same documents or workspace are shared, sensitive code or secrets can flow from Devin into external inference services through next-ai-draw-io, making the blast radius potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or document set, sensitive source code can be exposed.
IF next-ai-draw-io sends Devin-originated files to hosted model APIs, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared folder.
Disable cloud/API backends for sensitive documents.
Use a redaction step before handing files to next-ai-draw-io.
Separate credentials per agent and rotate exposed tokens.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin can write the filesystem, modify git state, and use broad network egress; next-ai-draw-io can call MCP and multiple model APIs. They overlap on mutable external resources and can race on shared files or integrations. The profiles do not prove a shared lock or coordination primitive, so the conflict is real but not high-confidence enough for high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repo or workspace, file and git conflicts can occur.
IF both agents invoke the same MCP-backed resource without locking, state races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories.
Serialize writes with a simple manual handoff.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Use branch protection for git operations.
requires-engineering: add distributed locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is an autonomous planner-executor that can act on browser, shell, and integrations, while next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted visualizations from documents. If Devin consumes next-ai-draw-io output as authoritative, a bad diagram or extracted fact can propagate into commits, tickets, or messages. That default-path handoff can cause multi-step downstream errors, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Devin uses next-ai-draw-io output as source-of-truth without verification, errors cascade.
IF the diagram tool summarizes a document incorrectly and Devin acts on it, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review before Devin acts on diagram-derived facts.
Mark next-ai-draw-io output as untrusted by default.
Cross-check extracted facts against the source document.
Limit Devin to drafting, not executing, for derived content.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and secrets in a vendor-managed cloud workspace; next-ai-draw-io sends documents to multiple external AI providers and handles API keys. If regulated or confidential documents are processed, residency and retention obligations may diverge across the pair. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency controls, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are routed through next-ai-draw-io’s hosted APIs, residency/retention obligations may be violated.
IF Devin stores team data in its cloud workspace while next-ai-draw-io retains prompts externally, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair until policies are confirmed.
Review vendor retention settings for both tools.
Use local-only models for sensitive documents.
Document a data-flow map for the shared workflow.
requires-engineering: obtain and enforce a DPA and residency controls.
